title: Greeting to the Church in Ephesus
english: Ignatius, who is also called God-Bearer, sends abundant greetings in Jesus Christ and in blameless joy to the church at Ephesus in Asia, a church most worthy of blessing. She is blessed in the greatness of God the Father in fullness, predestined before the ages to exist forever for abiding and unchangeable glory, united and chosen in true passion by the will of the Father and of Jesus Christ our God.
orientation: Ignatius, bishop of Antioch, opens his letter to the church in Ephesus with a formal greeting while being taken under guard to Rome.

title: Praise for the Ephesians' welcome and their bishop Onesimus
english: I welcomed your much-loved name in God, the name you possess through a righteous character according to faith and love in Christ Jesus our Savior. You are imitators of God; you rekindled the work that belongs to your kinship by the blood of God and completed it perfectly.

For when you heard that I had been bound from Syria for the sake of the common name and hope, and that I hoped through your prayer to succeed in fighting wild beasts in Rome, so that by succeeding I might be able to be a disciple, you hastened to see me.

Since, then, I have received your great multitude in the name of God in Onesimus, your bishop, whose love is beyond words, I pray that you love him according to Jesus Christ and that all of you be in likeness to him. Blessed is the one who granted you, being worthy, to have such a bishop.
orientation: Ignatius, bishop of Antioch, is writing as a prisoner on his way to martyrdom in Rome, and here he begins the body of his letter to the church at Ephesus by praising them for sending representatives to him.

title: Prayer for Burrhus and Crocus, and a call to unity under bishop and elders
english: Now about Burrhus, my fellow slave and your deacon in God's service, blessed in every way: I pray that he may remain with you for your honor and for the honor of the bishop. And Crocus, worthy of God and of you, whom I received as an example of the love that comes from you, refreshed me in every way. May the Father of Jesus Christ refresh him as well, along with Onesimus, Burrhus, Euplus, and Fronto, through whom I saw all of you in love.

May I have joy of you through all time, if only I am worthy. It is fitting, then, to glorify Jesus Christ in every way, for he has glorified you, so that you may be knit together in one submission, submitting to the bishop and the council of elders, and be sanctified in every way.
orientation: Ignatius, bishop of Antioch writing as a prisoner on his way to martyrdom in Rome, has just praised the Ephesian church and its bishop Onesimus, and now commends two more Ephesians, Burrhus and Crocus, before urging the whole church to be united under its bishop and council of elders.

title: Not commanding, but learning together
english: I am not giving you orders as if I were someone important. Even though I am bound in the Name, I am not yet perfected in Jesus Christ. Right now I am only beginning my training as a disciple, and I speak to you as to my fellow disciples. It was I who needed to be anointed by you with faith, admonition, endurance, and patience.

But since love does not allow me to keep silent about you, I have taken the initiative to urge you to run together with the purpose of God. For Jesus Christ, our inseparable life, is the purpose of the Father, just as the bishops appointed to the farthest bounds of the earth are in the purpose of Jesus Christ.
orientation: Ignatius, bishop of Antioch writing as a prisoner on his way to martyrdom in Rome, has just praised the Ephesians' unity under their bishop and now explains why he writes to them as a fellow learner rather than as an authority.

title: Harmony with the bishop as strings of a lyre
english: So you must align yourselves with the mind of the bishop, as you are already doing. Your council of elders, worthy of its name and worthy of God, is fitted together with the bishop as strings are fitted to a lyre. Because of this, in your concord and harmonious love, Jesus Christ is sung.

And let each of you become a choir, so that being in harmony and concord, having received the tuning of God in unity, you may sing with one voice through Jesus Christ to the Father, so that the Father may both hear you and recognize you, through the good you do, as members of his Son. It is useful, then, for you to be in blameless unity, so that you may always share in God.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Ephesus, urging them to align with their bishop Onesimus and the council of elders.

title: Unity with the bishop as unity with God
english: If I could enjoy such closeness with your bishop in so short a time, a closeness not merely human but spiritual, how much more do I count you blessed, who are as closely united with him as the church is with Jesus Christ, and as Jesus Christ is with the Father, so that all things may be in harmonious unity?

Let no one be deceived: if anyone is not within the altar, he is deprived of the bread of God. For if the prayer of one or two has such power, how much more does the prayer of the bishop and of the whole church?

So the one who does not come to the common assembly is already arrogant and has cut himself off. For it is written: "God opposes the arrogant" (Proverbs 3:34). Let us be eager, then, not to oppose the bishop, so that we may be subject to God.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Ephesus, urging them to remain united around their bishop, elders, and deacons, and now grounds this in his own brief but spiritual bond with their bishop Onesimus.

title: Honor the bishop as the one sent by the master
english: The more you see a bishop keeping silence, the more you should revere him. For everyone whom the master of the house sends to manage his own household, we must receive as we would receive the one who sent him. Clearly, then, we must regard the bishop as the Lord himself.

Onesimus himself praises your good order in God beyond measure, because you all live according to truth and because no false teaching dwells among you. Nor do you listen to anyone more than to Jesus Christ speaking in truth.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Ephesus, urging them to honor their bishop Onesimus as they would the Lord himself.

title: False teachers as rabid dogs; the one physician Jesus Christ
english: Some people, you see, have made a habit of carrying the name around with evil deceit while doing other things unworthy of God. You must shun them as you would wild beasts, for they are mad dogs that bite when you are not looking. Guard yourselves against them, because they are hard to heal.

There is one physician, both flesh and spirit, begotten and unbegotten, God in a human being, true life in death, both from Mary and from God, first subject to suffering and then beyond suffering: Jesus Christ our Lord.
orientation: Ignatius is warning the Ephesian church about false teachers who carry the name of Christ while acting unworthily, and then he confesses the paradoxical identity of Jesus Christ.

title: No one should deceive you; you live according to God
english: So let no one deceive you, just as you are not deceived, since you are wholly God's. For when no quarrel is entrenched among you that could torment you, then you are living according to God. I am an offering on your behalf, and I purify myself for you Ephesians, for the church renowned throughout the ages.

Fleshly people cannot do spiritual things, nor can spiritual people do fleshly things, just as faith cannot do the works of unbelief, nor unbelief the works of faith. Yet even what you do according to the flesh is spiritual, for in Jesus Christ you do all things.
orientation: Ignatius is addressing the church in Ephesus, urging them to remain united and free from strife as people wholly belonging to God.

title: The Ephesians as stones of the Father's temple
english: I have learned that certain people passed through from there carrying evil teaching, and you did not let them sow it among you. You plugged your ears so as not to receive what they were sowing, since you are stones of the Father's temple, prepared for the building of God the Father. You are being lifted up to the heights by the crane of Jesus Christ, which is the cross, with the Holy Spirit as the rope. Your faith is the crane that lifts you, and love is the road that carries you up to God.

So you are all fellow travelers, bearers of God and bearers of the temple, bearers of Christ, bearers of holy things, adorned in every way with the commandments of Jesus Christ. And I rejoice in these things, since I have been counted worthy through what I write to speak with you and to rejoice with you, because according to the life of humans you love nothing except God alone.
orientation: Ignatius is praising the Ephesian church for refusing to let false teachers sow their bad teaching among them, and he is describing their spiritual state as stones being lifted up to God.

title: Pray for others and answer evil with gentleness
english: Pray without ceasing for other people as well, because there is hope of repentance in them, so that they may attain God. Allow them, then, to learn from you at least through your works.

Toward their outbursts of anger, be gentle. Toward their boasts, be humble-minded. Toward their blasphemies, offer prayers. Toward their error, stand steadfast in faith. Toward their savagery, be mild, not eager to imitate them in return.

Let us be found to be their brothers by our gentleness, and let us be eager to be imitators of the Lord, asking who may be wronged more, who may be defrauded, who may be rejected, so that no weed of the devil may be found among you, but you may remain in Jesus Christ in all purity and self-control, in flesh and in spirit.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the Ephesians, urging them to pray for outsiders and to respond to hostility with Christlike gentleness rather than imitation.

title: Last times: fear God's patience or love his grace
english: These are the last times. From now on let us be ashamed, and let us fear the patience of God, so that it may not become judgment for us. Either let us fear the wrath that is coming, or let us love the grace that is present—one of the two. Only let us be found in Christ Jesus for the true life.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Ephesus, urging them to live in a way worthy of the last times, either fearing God's coming wrath or loving his present grace, so as to be found in Christ Jesus for true life.

title: Ignatius's bonds and Paul's example
english: Let nothing be fitting for you apart from this, in which I carry around my bonds, my chains, which are spiritual pearls. Through your prayer may I be granted to rise in them, and may I always share in that prayer, so that I may be found in the inheritance of the Ephesian Christians, who always agreed with the apostles in the power of Jesus Christ.
I know who I am and to whom I write. I am condemned; you have been shown mercy. I am under danger; you are established.

You are fellow-travelers with those being killed for God, fellow believers with Paul, who was sanctified, who bore witness, and who is worthy of blessing. May I be found in his footsteps when I attain God. In every letter he remembers you in Christ Jesus.
orientation: Ignatius, bishop of Antioch, is writing to the church in Ephesus while being taken under guard to Rome, and here he speaks of his chains and of Paul's memory of the Ephesians.

title: Frequent assembly defeats Satan
english: Make every effort, then, to gather more often for the Eucharist of God and for glory. For when you meet together frequently, the powers of Satan are torn down, and his ruin is dissolved by the unity of your faith.
Nothing is better than peace, in which every war of heavenly and earthly things is brought to nothing.
orientation: Ignatius is urging the Ephesians to gather more often for worship, continuing his praise of their unity with the apostles.

title: Faith and love as beginning and end
english: None of this escapes your notice, if you hold your faith and love in Jesus Christ perfectly. Faith is the beginning of life, and love is the end. The two, when they come together in unity, lead to God, and everything else follows toward goodness.

No one who professes faith sins, and no one who possesses love hates. A tree is visible by its fruit. So those who profess to belong to Christ will be seen by what they do. For the work is not now a matter of profession, but of being found in the power of faith to the end.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the Ephesians, urging them to hold faith and love toward Jesus Christ as the beginning and end of life.

title: Silence and action reveal the true disciple
english: It is better to be silent and to be, than to speak and not be. Teaching is good, if the one who speaks also does. There is one teacher, who spoke and it came to be; and the things he has done in silence are worthy of the Father.
The one who truly possesses the word of Jesus is able to hear even his silence, so that he may be perfect, so that through what he speaks he acts, and through what he is silent about he is known.

Nothing escapes the Lord's notice; even our hidden things are near to him. Let us therefore do everything as if he dwells in us, so that we may be his temples and he may be in us as our God. This is indeed the case, and it will appear before our face, because of which we rightly love him.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the Ephesians, urging them to be true disciples whose deeds match their words, because God dwells in them.

title: Warning against corrupters of the faith
english: Do not be deceived, my brothers: those who destroy households will not inherit the kingdom of God.

If those who practice these things according to the flesh have died, how much more will the one who corrupts the faith of God with evil teaching, the faith for which Jesus Christ was crucified? Such a person, having become filthy, will go into the unquenchable fire, and the one who listens to him will do the same.
orientation: Ignatius is warning the Ephesians about false teachers who corrupt the faith, continuing his argument that believers must live as temples of God.

title: The Lord's ointment and the gift of knowledge
english: This is why the Lord received anointing on his head: so that he might breathe incorruption into the church. Do not anoint yourselves with the foul odor of the teaching of the ruler of this age, lest he take you captive from the life set before you.
Why do we not all become wise, since we have received the knowledge of God, which is Jesus Christ? Why do we perish foolishly, failing to recognize the gift that the Lord has truly sent?
orientation: Ignatius is warning the Ephesians against false teachers who corrupt faith, and now explains why the Lord received ointment on his head and why believers should accept the knowledge of God.

title: The Cross as Wisdom and the Incarnation of Jesus
english: My spirit is an expiation of the cross, which is a stumbling block to those who disbelieve, but to us it is salvation and eternal life. Where is the wise person? Where is the debater? Where is the boasting of those called intelligent?

For our God, Jesus the Christ, was carried in the womb by Mary according to the plan of God, from the seed of David on the one hand, but of the Holy Spirit on the other. He was born and baptized so that by his passion he might purify the water.
orientation: Ignatius, writing to the Ephesians, is contrasting the cross as the true wisdom of God with the empty wisdom of the world, and then states the incarnation and baptism of Jesus.

title: Three mysteries hidden from the ruler of this age
english: The virginity of Mary, her giving birth, and the death of the Lord escaped the notice of the ruler of this age. These are three mysteries proclaimed aloud, yet accomplished in the silence of God.
How then was he revealed to the ages?

A star shone in heaven above all the stars, and its light was unspeakable, and its newness caused astonishment. All the rest of the stars, together with the sun and moon, became a chorus for the star, and it surpassed them all in light. And there was confusion: where did this new thing, so unlike them, come from?

From that moment all sorcery was being dissolved and every bond of wickedness was being made to disappear. Ignorance was being torn down, the ancient kingdom of evil was being destroyed, as God was being revealed in human form for the newness of eternal life. What had been fully prepared with God was now beginning. From then on all things were being stirred together, because the destruction of death was being set in motion.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the Ephesians, explaining how the virginity, birth, and death of Jesus were hidden from the devil and then revealed to the ages through the star.

title: The second letter and the medicine of immortality
english: If Jesus Christ considers me worthy through your prayers, and if it is His will, I will explain to you in the second little book that I intend to write to you the plan I have begun to set forth concerning the new man, Jesus Christ, in His faith and in His love, in His passion and resurrection.

I will do this especially if the Lord reveals to me that you all, man by man, come together by name in grace, in one faith and in Jesus Christ, who according to the flesh is from the line of David, the son of man and Son of God, so that you obey the bishop and the council of elders with undistracted mind, breaking one bread, which is the medicine of immortality, the antidote so that we do not die but live in Jesus Christ forever.
orientation: Ignatius is closing his letter to the Ephesians, promising a second letter and describing the unity he hopes to hear about among them.

title: Closing exchange of souls and farewell
english: I am a ransom for you and for those you sent to Smyrna for the honor of God. From Smyrna I am also writing to you, giving thanks to the Lord and loving Polycarp as I love you. Remember me, as Jesus Christ also remembers you.

Pray for the church in Syria, from where I am being led away to Rome in chains, though I am the least of the faithful there, just as I was counted worthy to be found for the honor of God. Farewell in God the Father and in Jesus Christ, our common hope.
orientation: Ignatius is closing his letter to the Ephesians, speaking of himself as their ransom and asking their prayers for the church in Syria as he is taken to Rome.
